issues.description: Template method name for the 3-qubit QFT does not match the solution and the exercise expectation: the template defines _qft_circuit(...) while the solution and the problem tasks expect qft_circuit(...). This name/signature mismatch is structural and will confuse students and tests that call qft_circuit. Students may implement the wrong method name or tests may fail to find the implemented QFT routine.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method _qft_circuit to qft_circuit and ensure its signature (qc: QuantumCircuit) and return type match the solution and the exercise description. Update any references in the template so students implement qft_circuit(...) as required by the tests.

issues.description: The Problem Statement and Solution refer to a public QFT constructor method named qft_circuit for the 3-qubit QFT exercise, but the Template declares the method with a leading underscore as _qft_circuit. This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual operation (the 3-qubit QFT implementation) can confuse students and break automated tests that expect qft_circuit to exist and be implemented.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method _qft_circuit to qft_circuit (remove the leading underscore) so the template, problem statement, and solution use the same public method name. Also ensure qft_circuit_inverse calls or reuses qft_circuit consistently.
